previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with an acute flare characterized by epigastric pain, nausea, and poor oral intake. She also reported new right lower quadrant pain, likely due to adhesions, though imaging showed no obstruction. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. A PICC line was placed on hospital day 3, and TPN was initiated on day 4 to support nutrition. Her lipase normalized, pain improved, and she advanced to a regular diet. Pancytopenia was noted but stable, presumed related to malnutrition, with plans for outpatient follow-up. Constipation was treated with increased bowel regimen. She remained on home medications for depression, overactive bladder, and GERD. She was discharged home with a 3-week TPN plan, visiting nurse services, and follow-up arranged with her GI and primary care providers.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yoF with a history of GERD, idiopathic chronic pancreatitis 
s/p recent admission for chronic pancreatitis (___), 
started on TPN presents with ongoing abdominal pain.

# ABDOMINAL PAIN, CHRONIC PANCREATITIS: She presented with 
persistent symptoms, worsened after food intake. Her LFTs and 
lipase were normal on exam.  She had MRCP with no significant 
change but recommended 12 month follow-up due to several small 
cystic lesions and dilated side ducts.  She was kept on TPN and 
IV pain medications.  Her diet attempted to be advanced several 
times but she had worsening of her pain.  She eventually was 
kept only on sips and her pain improved.  She was changed to 
oral pain medications with good effect.  Her fentanyl patch was 
also increased during admission to 100mcg/hr.

# DEPRESSION:  Home medications were continued.  

# ANEMIA:  Microcytic, chronic.  Markedly iron deficient with 
ferritin of 9.  Would consider IV iron supplementation as an 
outpatient.  She should also have a colonoscopy as an 
outpatient.

# CONSTIPATION: She had significant constipation during 
admission likely related to her increased dosing of narcotics.  
She should continue a bowel regimen for constipation.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
- Needs weekly CBC/diff, LFTs, Chem10 given TPN administration 
- Has GI follow-up for advancement of diet and reassessment
- Found to have stable small cystic lesions/dilated side 
branches in the pancreatic body and tail, measuring up to 6 mm, 
unchanged.  Recommend followup imaging in 12 months.
